assessment: Two harvest passes emptied this pool of upgrades, and the v3 facts confirm it: the primary win is now checker-verified end to end (stack 006, 15-cast minimum from 32 life), its one verified weakness — fully open priority windows on every loop cast and every Reservoir activation — is shielded by the card the last pass promoted (Grand Abolisher, now maindeck), and the five approved swaps landed with the two-piece at 41.3%, wincon access at 50.1%, and the floor at 4 on nine Game Changers. I evaluated every remaining angle the pool offers against the verified engines — a fourth loop rock, the Omniscience package, Laboratory Maniac redundancy, an Abolisher backup, and a return case for each of the five departed cards — and none earns a slot. Zero swaps: the 60 analysable pool cards are now purely conditional tech and spares, which is what a sideboard behind a verified, protected primary line should be.

opens_lines.why_plausible: Stack 006's verified caveat is that every loop cast and every 'Pay 50 life' activation opens a fully open priority window on an unshielded board. Abolisher's text — opponents can't cast spells or activate abilities of artifacts, creatures, or enchantments during your turn — appears to close all of them, but channel abilities (Otawara, Soaring City) are activated from a card in hand, not from an artifact, creature, or enchantment permanent, so whether the 15-cast line is airtight under Abolisher, and against exactly what, needs its own walkthrough.

Jace's static replaces the empty-library draw with a win and the maindeck X-draw suite self-targeted presents that draw, with Archive and Teferi's Ageless Insight roughly halving the X needed — but the layered replacement of Archive's draw-two against Jace's win mid-resolution, and what happens if Jace leaves the battlefield partway through, must be walked through. This scenario also decides Laboratory Maniac's entire sideboard value.

A free Approach under Omniscience is still cast from hand, Heliod's per-opponent-draw discount plus the table-draw density can realistically pay {7}{U}{U}{U}, and free countermagic then defends the second cast. Unverified: cast-from-hand satisfaction under an alternative cost, the win-check timing, and the cost that every X-spell resolves at X=0 when cast free under it.

Commanders killed by Supreme Verdict or exiled by Path elect the command zone (CR 903.9) and Drannith makes casting from there illegal — but bounce from Hullbreaker Horror or Cyclonic Rift goes to hand, which Drannith does not stop, so the lock's real coverage needs the 903.9 walkthrough before it is played as fact.

Fraying Sanity triggers at the beginning of the end step, before cleanup discards happen, so whether Fruition-bloated trim-to-7 discards ever count (including via a repeated cleanup under CR 514.3) is a genuine open rules question that decides whether the curse doubles the punisher engine or misses it entirely.

long_term_defaults.why: Not a fourth loop rock and not a return case: the 004 ledger's mana-neutrality requires an untapped rock whose cast cost is covered by same-turn production, and Powerstone enters tapped — every bounce-recast cycle pays {3} and produces nothing until your next turn, a strictly mana-negative link. Outside the loop it is still the slowest of the deck's rocks on a 57-blue-pip base.

The return case fails on the same arithmetic that cut it: stack 004's ledger showed it recasts mana-negative ({4} in, {C}{C} out, -2 per cycle), and its draw rider fires only if an X-spell follows the same turn — the loop casts no X-spells.

The pool's only other ramp body cannot touch the loop at all: both of its abilities restrict the mana to instant or sorcery spells, and every spell the 004/006 engine casts is an artifact — its mana is illegal for every loop piece.

Still the pool's biggest unresolved upside, and v3 cuts both ways: Grand Abolisher in the 99 answers the old no-protection objection, but stack 006's verification means the deck no longer needs a second, unverified nine-mana package — a slot spent on Omniscience now displaces a card that supports the proven line. Verdict unchanged until the Approach scenario resolves; if it verifies favourably, re-argue then.

Redundancy for a line that is itself still unverified is redundancy for nothing yet: until the Jace/X-draw scenario passes, Maniac is a 2/2 with no other function that dies to any removal mid-draw. Even after verification he enters behind Jace, who draws cards on his own; sleeve Maniac only in pods where a resolved Jace has proven a removal magnet.

The return case fails against 006's verified weakness: the open windows lose to removal on any of four pieces and to instant-speed plays generally, and Greaves equips only creatures — it covers Hullbreaker Horror against targeted removal and does nothing for Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, or Aetherflux Reservoir, none of which it can hold. Grand Abolisher closes the windows wholesale for the same two mana.

The v3 goldfish reproduces the decay that cut it: land-drop hit rate 57.2% at t5 and 48.2% at t6, exactly when the engine must be online, while maindeck Jace Beleren draws each player unconditionally and survives the artifact sweep that takes the Mine effects.

The v3 plan still includes casting your own Supreme Verdict, which wipes Mentor's monk board along with everything else; Teferi, Temporal Pilgrim converts the same spell velocity into loyalty that your own wrath never touches. Nothing in v3 reopens this.

Explicitly not a Grand Abolisher backup: its statics stop counterspells only, while 006's open windows are lost to removal and instant-speed plays that no uncounterability prevents — and a Reservoir activation is not a cast, so Sphinx protects nothing in the window that matters. It remains counter-war tech for three-plus-blue-seat pods.

The read-the-card check on the pool's last cast-payoff candidate: its Opus trigger fires only on instant or sorcery casts, and the verified loop casts artifact spells exclusively — an unbounded 006 turn gives it zero triggers. The pool contains no second payoff that keys on the loop's cast count; Aetherflux Reservoir stands alone.

gaps: No Grand Abolisher redundancy exists anywhere in the pool: no other card restricts what opponents may do during your turn, so the verified kill's one shield has no backup — if Abolisher is answered, the fallback is the maindeck free-counter suite guarding up to fifteen open windows by hand. Settling whether that suite realistically holds the line is a coaching/scenario question; acquiring a redundant effect is outside this analysis's constraint and is flagged for the pilot as the deck's one real structural exposure.

The Abolisher-closes-006 claim is asserted in strategic_frame from oracle text but has no checker-passed walkthrough; the channel-land loophole (Otawara activates from hand, not from an artifact/creature/enchantment) is the specific thing a scenario must scope before the shield is played as airtight.

The strategy corpus still has no sections on group-slug donation risk, blink value engines, or hand-size as an attack vector (per strategic_frame.gaps), so the punisher-adjacent judgments above rest on oracle text, the verified stacks, and the v3 goldfish rather than citable principles.

The two-piece rate (41.3% by t6) still cannot be raised from the sideboard: the pool contains zero punisher-half effects, and the engine-half redundancy it did contain (Jace Beleren) is already maindeck.
